title: Cluster computing: nodes, scheduler and fault tolerance

videos.script: A cluster is four kinds of process, and only one of them is yours. {{roles}} The driver is your program. It plans the job and hands out the tasks. The master rents out cores and then steps aside. Workers offer a machine's cores and memory, and executors do the work. {{processes}} This lesson starts a job, lists every process it made, and then kills them one at a time. {{kill}} Kill an executor and the job barely notices. The lost task runs again somewhere else. Kill a worker and the job finishes, slower, on what is left. {{worker}} Kill the driver and everything is gone. And the master calls it finished. {{driver}} On one computer, a broken disk is an event. On a thousand, something breaks every day. {{weather}} So a cluster is built to notice a loss, know what it took, and redo only that. By the end of this lesson you will have watched it do all three, and seen the one case it cannot save. {{end}}
